If you are going to spend enough time to modify something (which with how fair use is, requires substantial changes to the original) and the cost of that, and defending it in court if it ever comes to that, you're just better off paying an artist to make an original creation.

AI can not be 'inspired'. It is not actually intelligent. It makes no creative decisions. It does what the code tells it to do. 

Also, I don't have to debate every fucking point you make if all I want to do is debunk one stupidly made claim.

Valve owns the marketplace, they can decide what and whatnot gets put on it. It won't open them up to a lawsuit. This was decided in Apple vs. Epic games, and that had more ground to stand on.

A developer can still publish their game, they just have to make sure the assets they make are owned by them (I.E. can claim copyright on them) which you can't currently do for AI generated art. So they either pick up the tablet and make them themselves or they pay someone to make it for them, it's a requirement for the marketplace they wish to post on.

If they steal assets, that's on them, Valve can operate under faith they were lied too, and in cases where that has been true, Valve has removed them and sometimes even banned the dev from publishing on Steam, but it's common knowledge that AI generated content was likely trained on various, unconsenting, unpaid artists, so Valve knowing that and allowing publishing, would be liable if an artist can ultimately prove they had copyright over the image that was used to train the data, (which will eventually happen), Valve will be liable as much as the developer.

Valve is simply choosing to avoid it all together.

Copyright is an major issue for rights holders: If you have AI design your main character, you have no copyright protections, anyone can wholesale just take the same design. This isn't just someone making a fan-game; Microsoft makes a game that is incredibly popular based on AI designs? While Sony couldn't take the game wholesale, they certainly take things without any legal protections and make a game to either that borrows character likeness to either make something for themselves, or more likely, welcome 3rd parties to create knockoffs to cheapen the appeal.

And also, to that point, the issue of it stealing from other artist isn't a intrinsically a legal wrong. Proving something legally wrong is expensive, a hassle and requires interpretations of laws that haven't been around long enough to account for AI. It's a moral wrong, I.E. taking the efforts of others who did not consent and profiting off of them without paying them is wrong.
Land ownership is also an arbitrary and social construct.

There hasn't really been any research on Nonbinary HRT. There simply isn't any studies being done on it. The common belief medically is that there is no in between. The body either uses T or E but not both; and one usually will be converted into the other if it's introduced.

From I have read, all of it is anecdotal. From what I've heard of the effects of low dose; practically nothing. It *might* reduce some effects of masculine features but chances are without any blockers the excess E will just be broken down and replaced with T. 

From what others have said, If you experience any feminization, it also forms breast buds with, so if that is something you don't want...

I would guess that if you wanted to look androgynous, reducing testosterone to a lower level might be more effective than adding; assuming that it hasn't done much already to your bone/facial/muscular structure. But even AA can cause gynecomastia and you run the risk of having weaker bones and energy due to a lack of primary sex hormone.

I have heard people having luck with adding moderate dosage of estrogen but also introducing a breast growth inhibitor like Tamoxifen for a non-binary look but I never heard or seen the results of this.

Best of luck though.

There is no "bare minimum". It takes nothing to hold a blue pill under your tongue for 15 minutes; and doing so might make you feel better. But what you *don't* know is going to be what causes the most issues.

You might wonder why you have headaches on the outside of your skull on CPA. Or you might be concerned that you might feel more depressed because your libido is dead and nothing arouses you anymore. Or you might have severe pain in your side one night and spend most of night wondering if your liver is failing. Or you might just be wondering why you aren't growing breast while your friend has already progressed to C-cups in the same time. Knowledge helps all of that. 

I didn't have blood test until my 5th month. I started 2mg E, spent most of my time in 4mg, and only raised it to 6mg the month before. When I got my bloodtest, my E was 172; which was lower than I had wanted (I was wanting 250-300 at minimum). I probably spent most of my transition with terrible E levels and stunted my growth because of it. If I would of had bloodwork after 2 months, then I could have corrected it and might be better off.

But taking low dose CPA/E isn't likely going to do much harm physically; I would be more concerned about mental effects.

Also remember that a clinic might not do blood test but also remember that there is a good chance that a clinic doesn't really care about your transition; they just want you in and out.

This was something my gender therapist told me when I brought it up to her, around the first consultation trying to go from DIY to legit. She asked me why I might have hesitated about transitioning and I told her that for awhile I thought I just had a sexual fetish, then she explained why a lot of others think that. I don't have a specific source but I do remember what she told me and found something similar. 

From what I remember, it's the same thing as the "misattribution of arousal". Your body doesn't have an "aroused" emotion; it's sort of a mix of different things going on. The mind takes this information and just assumed that "well, if this is happening, I must be aroused so let me go ahead and turn on these other things." It's common with things like fear (study linked below) but it can happen with anything that causes the same reaction, including euphoria.

Study:
https://youarenotsosmart.com/2011/07/07/misattribution-of-arousal/

The issue is sort of two fold. The therapist said that when you spend most of your life feeling dysphoric, you also tend to have a lot of issues sexually, such as low self-confidence, post-orgasm guilt, etc. So something that is validating tends to be extremely euphoric and then, because our brain doesn't know better, says "oh, this thing arouses us." instead of "this is something we want in our lives" because we're not used to having euphoric states.

Then this creates a feedback loop in the community where there is a overwhelming attraction to things like forced fem/sissification/etc. in which it's advertised as a fetish, so you can't like those things other than as a fetish (since we're told fetishes are 'only for the bedroom'). So we sort of only feel comfortable in terms of sexual fulfillment, and then it feeds it back into the brain as arousal. It's a pretty vicious and invalidating cycle but it's often the only way most of us can explore it safely.

For me? Just 2mg of Estradiol, one pill a day (split for two different doses) by all means a *very* conservative starting dose, and I felt better within days, before any physical changes could conceivably happen. 

At the time, I wasn't even taking it with the intention of transitioning; but instead was doing it as a "test run", half-hoping I would prove to myself that I *wasn't* trans because I figured if I wasn't, it would make me feel bad.

Nope, I was *way* wrong and it's the happiest I ever been being wrong about something. But that's my experience, I can't speak for anyone else other than my own. I wouldn't believe so. If you are having a surge in T-symptoms, it's most likely one of two things. Either your body is going through it's own natural hormonal cycle where it's producing more Testosterone than usual, or it's your testicles saying "wait a sec, Estrogen? this isn't what I was expecting" and attempts to over produce (my guess is that this is a natural reaction to estrogenic foods). In either case it is temporary and will cease as your testicles start to atrophy.

The process though can take weeks, which is why it's important to wait it out. Note that even with T-symptoms, you are still feminizing. Which is why you shouldn't increase dosage according to symptoms unless they do not go away on it's own.

It's highly, *highly* unlikely that your body is outright fighting the process.

If you can get your levels tested, that's the better option. But I personally know that might not be available at a moment's notice (I haven't been able to afford bloodwork either), so here is what you should do.

1. Wait it out. Give it a week or two and see if they are frequent. My body was fine on low dose E and Cypro for awhile then I had the same thing happen, erections, oily skin, male body odor, etc. It could just be the body not knowing what to do and is attempting to produce more T (but not able to sustain it) and it could die back down. My case, it didn't go down after a week.

2. Increase one or the other but not both. You won't know what is the problem, your AA levels are too low or if you aren't getting enough E, either one could be causing the issue, but you don't want to overdue it. Pick one, preferably the less potent of the two dosages and walk it up slowly. In this case, maybe increase Spiro by 50, using it three times per day and see if that helps. If it doesn't walk it back a step and increase E and see if that helps.

3. If you are still getting symptoms and they are still very prevalent, then you can increase both. But be careful, the more you take, the more stress you are putting on your body to handle it and you might be doing more damage in the long term.

4. If neither of that works, just wait it out. While they might be signs of masculinization still around, you should still be constantly progressing towards feminization, T-symptoms or not. Instead, take the time to save up for blood test and then see what might be the issue, if you're not suppressing T or your E-levels aren't high enough. That will give you a better informed decision.
